display.title: Episode 528: The Rambam's Grave, Chapter 1
display.summary_short: Why the Rebbe called it Tzivos Hashem, a four-year-old's Shema, the life of the Rambam and the mystery of where he would be buried, a listener's letter, and humility from Pirkei Avos.
display.summary_long: Uncle Yossi explains why the Rebbe named the children's club Tzivos Hashem: exile is like darkness, and every soldier's mission is to bring light through Torah and mitzvos until Moshiach comes and swords are turned into plowshares. Before story time he explains the name Rambam, Rabbeinu Moshe ben Maimon, and a four-year-old kindergarten boy recites the Shema, followed by tzedakah. The story tells the Rambam's life: born in Cordova on Erev Pesach, forced to flee as a boy, wandering to Morocco, surviving a storm at sea on the way to Eretz Yisroel, praying at the Kosel and the Me'aras HaMachpelah, and finally settling in Egypt, where he wrote the Mishneh Torah and the Thirteen Principles of Faith. Before he passed away he asked to be buried in Eretz Yisroel without saying where, and representatives of Yerushalayim, Chevron and Meron each claim the honor. A mysterious miracle is about to settle it, next week. A girl's letter asks how to join Tzivos Hashem. The show ends with Pirkei Avos: good character comes before Torah, Moshe learned humility from Har Sinai, and the Jews camped there 'like one person with one heart'.
display.lesson: Bring light into the world through Torah and mitzvos, and be humble and united like the Jews at Har Sinai.
